programme: No single module is defensible. The concordant set splits across at least six unrelated functional families with no shared complex or convergent targets: an IκB-family NF-κB inhibitor (NFKBIB, whose 'targets' — TNF, IL1B, IKBKB, CHUK, MAP3K14, CXCL8, CCL5, PTGS2, NOS2, SOD2, PLAU — read as NF-κB pathway genes, even though IκBβ itself is a cytoplasmic sequestering protein, not a DNA-binding factor); an ER-stress/UPR bZIP (CREB3); a cluster of cardiac/pituitary/gonadal developmental homeodomain and bHLH factors (PITX2, IRX4, ZFPM2, HESX1, HEY1) whose targets are largely heart-morphogenesis genes (GATA4, MYH6/7, NPPB, MYOCD, NOTCH1/2/4); an imprinted growth/autophagy regulator (PEG3, targeting BECN1, MAP1LC3A, TP53); a glucose-sensing bHLH-Zip (MLXIP, targeting LDHA, PFKFB3, TXNIP); a cell-cycle-linked factor (STOX1, targeting CCNA2/B1/C/E1); an HLH differentiation inhibitor (ID4); and a nuclear receptor coactivator (NCOA6). None of these targets sets overlap with each other in a way that suggests one pathway, and PITX2's 103 inferred targets (versus 4-28 for the others) look like a generically well-connected hub rather than a specific programme member.
role_in_a: Individually, several factors have fragmentary NSCLC literature (CREB3 in ER-stress-driven malignancy, PEG3 via a microRNA axis, IRX4 via a stem-like resistance phenotype, PITX2 in tumour progression/anti-autophagy, HEY1 in EMT/cisplatin resistance, ID4 as an NSCLC biomarker), but these are disconnected mechanisms in different papers, not one programme operating together in lung cancer.
role_in_b: No role can be stated. Ten of the twelve factors have no Open Targets association with Sjögren's syndrome at all, CREB3 sits at an unremarkable mid percentile (0.60), and not one retrieved paper places any of these twelve factors in Sjögren's syndrome.
shared_axis: None can be written responsibly. There is no retrieved or inferable mechanism connecting a cardiac-developmental homeodomain cluster, an NF-κB inhibitor, an ER-stress factor, and a metabolic sensor to salivary/lacrimal gland autoimmunity, and forcing one would mean inventing a story the factors don't support.
reasoning: The factors do not cluster into a nameable complex or pathway — they span cardiac development, NF-κB inhibition, ER stress, glucose sensing, imprinting/autophagy, and cell-cycle control with no target overlap between them. Disease-B evidence is essentially null (10/12 factors have no Open Targets signal and zero literature hits for Sjögren's), and disease-A evidence is thin, scattered across single unconnected papers per factor rather than converging on one mechanism, so there is nothing here to build a shared-axis claim on.
support: 35720482 (CREB3/SEC61G in ER-stress-driven lung cancer progression, disease A only); 33898106 (PEG3 via MTTL3/miR-1246 in NSCLC, disease A only); 32820157 (IRX4 in vitamin-D-linked NSCLC stemness, disease A only); 34765299 (PITX2 in lung cancer progression/anti-autophagy, disease A only); 39696915 and 36396748 (HEY1 as a lung adenocarcinoma driver gene and in cisplatin resistance, disease A only); 41691850 (ID4 as an NSCLC biomarker, disease A only); 25982285 (NFKBIB listed in a chromosome-19 lung cancer genotype study, weak/indirect). None of these address Sjögren's syndrome or any relationship between the factors; 'none found' for the shared axis itself.
how_to_falsify: Test whether any subset of these factors physically co-occupies a shared set of loci (ChIP-seq/Cut&Run co-binding, or co-IP for complex formation) in a lung or salivary-gland cell line — if two or more genuinely converge on the same targets, a module claim becomes testable. Separately, assay any one factor (e.g., NFKBIB/NF-κB activity, or CREB3/UPR markers) in Sjögren's-syndrome salivary gland biopsies or PBMCs; a positive, reproducible signal there would overturn the 'no disease-B evidence' basis for the incoherent call.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood (Sjögren's) vs lung (cancer) — different compartments with no a priori reason to share a developmental-TF programme. The 196 patient-group comparisons rest on only 2 independent cohort pairs, so high concordance counts (e.g. NFKBIB 102/196, CREB3 112/196) largely reflect repeated clinical substratification of the same two cohorts rather than independent replication, and should not be read as strong cross-cohort validation. The single-view exclusions (IRX2, HOXD8, GATA2, TET1, NCOR1, etc.) show the ranking is already sensitive to which subgroup is examined, and the tissue-generic exclusions (EBF1, GFI1, TAL1, BCL6, TWIST1, etc.) removed the expected blood/immune master regulators — meaning what remains is not tissue-generic, but it also never coheres into a specific alternative story.
